column3: Near-identical local precedent: a messenger among his people gives the same exclusive-worship and mindfulness call.
Shows the messenger's protective, accessible posture toward followers, supporting the focus's in-community mission.
Applies mindfulness of God to protecting others from public humiliation, adding an ethical consequence to the call.
Repeats the prophetic address and exact worship formula for another people, confirming its recurring mission pattern.
The immediate transition to another generation situates the focus within a succession of communities.
Extends mindfulness of God into an enduring, whole-life commitment beyond the focus's imperative.
Noah's matching call supplies an earlier messenger precedent and explicitly adds warning of a great day.
The same-surah limit on every community's term frames the larger sequence but not the focus's call itself.
Affirms a messenger identity but adds neither in-community origin nor the worship command.
Repeats the exclusive-worship address while casting its rejection as fabrication, adding a contrary reception.
Revelation, judgment, and distinct communal laws give only a broad setting for divine guidance through a messenger.
The denial of shared worship marks a boundary around exclusive devotion, though it lacks the messenger setting.
Sending punishment after altered speech does not clarify the sending or call in the focus.
The immediate response rejects the messenger as merely human, directly testing the focus's messenger-from-among-them claim.
The exclusion of failed paths only loosely parallels the focus's exclusive direction of worship.
The same worship formula joins creation, cultivation, repentance, and response, expanding its practical horizon.
The immediate sequel presents messengers sent in succession and communities repeatedly denying them, explaining the focus's place in that cadence.
Sending the she-camel as a test uses a different object and does not illuminate the messenger's call.
Explicitly asks for a messenger raised among the people, directly clarifying the focus's in-community messenger.
A deferred decree and appointed term do not clarify the worship call or messenger origin.
Mindfulness tied to the Fire supplies a consequence but adds little after the direct call examples.
Addresses all people with worship of their creating Lord so that they may become mindful, closely joining the focus's two imperatives.
The immediate elite objection makes obedience to a human peer the contested issue raised by the focus's messenger-from-them wording.
Guidance and misguidance in the cave narrative do not clarify the focus's mission or command.
Generalizes the focus's structure: every community receives a messenger commanding worship of God and rejection of false powers.
The nearby statement of signs and testing supplies a broad frame for the preceding Noah narrative.
Pairs piety with obedience to the messenger, but applies it to private consultation rather than the focus's proclamation.
Same-surah acknowledgment of God's lordship culminates in the exact exhortation to mindfulness.
Dispute over Moses's scripture and deferred judgment do not add to this messenger-and-worship formulation.
Commands cooperation in piety and mindfulness, a practical but distant application of the focus's closing exhortation.
Sending a flood as punishment is not comparable to sending a messenger to call a people.
The immediate audience's objection shifts from the human messenger to disbelief in resurrection, showing their broader resistance.
A general appeal to mindfulness for mercy lacks the focus's exclusive-worship and messenger structure.
A messenger reports that his sole command was worship of God as shared Lord, closely paralleling the focus's message.
Belief in the Lord's signs is a later same-surah response trait, but it does not develop the focus's address.
Avoiding the worship of false powers and turning to God gives a concrete counterpart to the focus's denial of any other god.
Explicitly describes a messenger raised from among the believers and details his recitation, purification, and teaching functions.
The accidental-killing repair sequence does not clarify the focus's messenger or monotheistic call.
The challenge concerning human power at death does not bear on the focus's message.
Sending a destructive wind concerns punishment, not a messenger's in-community call.
The immediate dismissal of what is promised continues the local narrative of rejection without specifying the call.
God's uniqueness and knowledge support monotheism generally but add no messenger or responsive dimension.
Sending plagues after arrogance is a punitive sending rather than the focus's prophetic sending.
Inheritance of scripture and differing recipients do not clarify the focus's address.
Divine justice toward servants only broadly relates to the accountability implied by rejecting the message.
Sending wind and unseen forces in battle does not illuminate the messenger's call.
The immediate denial of resurrection reveals the community's disbelief, but not the content of 23:32 directly.
The creation challenge supports divine authority only indirectly, without the focus's missionary form.
Acknowledgment of God's creative governance ends in the same call to mindfulness, grounding its monotheistic basis.
Giving Moses the Book follows the messenger cycle but does not add to this specific call.
A rule about lawful sexual relations has no material connection to the focus.
A messenger sent among an unlettered people supplies a close parallel to the focus's messenger from among them and adds teaching functions.
The fixed term of communities resonates with the surrounding succession motif, not the focus's message.
Calling Solomon an excellent returning servant gives only a distant model of devotion.
The discussion of the cave companions' number does not clarify the focus.
The immediate accusation that the messenger invents a lie directly records rejection of the focus's proclamation.
The exception for devoted servants gives only a loose link to worship.
Describes modes of divine communication, including sending a messenger, but not the focus's communal call.
The following blast is unrelated to prophetic dispatch or exclusive worship.
Reward for believers doing good does not clarify the focus's messenger or command.
The better Hereafter for the mindful gives a distant consequence of piety without the focus's mission structure.
The messenger's immediate appeal for help after being denied supplies the next stage of resistance to the focus's call.
Defines the Prophet's sending as mercy for all worlds, enriching the purpose of being sent while differing in audience scope.
The tactical prayer formation does not clarify the sending or monotheistic proclamation.
The next dispatch in the same sequence confirms ongoing prophetic succession but adds little after 23:44.
Corrects an assertion about God by identifying honored servants, only loosely related to worship.
A messenger sent to his kin with the worship command leads to division, adding a reception outcome to the recurring formula.
Rejects the novelty of the messenger and limits him to revelation and warning, but is less direct than earlier parallels.
Repeats the earlier nonshared-worship statement without adding to its relevance.
The shared worship formula is extended to honest measure and balance, showing its social demands.
The promise of the deniers' regret is a local consequence after the focus's rejection.
Sending devils against disbelievers is not comparable to sending a messenger from among a people.
The same worship formula connects to social justice and reform, a fuller ethical expansion than the earlier repetition.
The address to messengers about lawful provision and good works gives a later same-surah instruction, not their public call.
Prior messengers bringing clear proofs and vindication of believers broadly support the prophetic pattern.
The repeated formula is followed by a specific sign and warning, but the central formulation is already well established.
Scripture as confirmation, warning, and good news only generally relates to a messenger's guidance.
The difficulty for disbelievers does not clarify the focus's message or sender.
States that every messenger is sent in his people's language to make matters clear, directly explaining the accessibility implied by a messenger from among them.
Another generation after them reinforces the same-surah succession frame without developing the focus.
The opening mention of mercy to Zechariah does not clarify the focus.
Prior messengers with families and limited signs confirm their human continuity, but add little to the focus's call.
The same-surah assertion that truth came to them and they lie gives a later verdict on their rejection.
Messengers sent to a town and denied show a similar dispatch-and-rejection pattern, though without the focus's message.
Combines worship of God and mindfulness with obedience to the messenger, closely completing the focus's imperative sequence.
Warnings against following Satan do not clarify the focus's prophetic call despite a general moral overlap.
Opposing the messenger after guidance and following another path gives a consequence for rejecting the message, but is distant.
Abraham's address to his people explicitly joins worship of God and mindfulness, closely repeating the focus's core command.
Noah's request for a blessed landing does not clarify the later messenger's proclamation.
God as the wisest judge supports divine authority only generally.
Proclaims one God who gives life and death and calls for faith in His messenger, joining monotheism with messenger-following.
Moses and Aaron identify themselves as their Lord's messengers while seeking liberation, but the mission differs from the focus's call.
The bare self-identification as messengers of the Lord adds little beyond other messenger statements.
The objection to abandoning ancestral gods directly displays resistance to exclusive worship, though it is only a fragment.
God's limits in fasting aim at mindfulness, a legal application far from the focus's missionary address.
Acknowledging God as creator yet lacking understanding exposes the gap between recognition and the focus's required worship.
The morning cry that seized a people does not clarify the focus's sending or call.
Calling the Prophet a messenger and God as witness gives a general mission affirmation without the focus's communal formula.
Divine knowledge of concealed and public speech does not clarify the focus.
Human willing remains under God, Lord of all worlds, only broadly supporting the authority behind the focus's command.
States the universal prophetic pattern directly: every messenger receives the revelation that no god exists but God and that He alone is to be worshipped.
Combines God's exclusive divinity with the direct command to worship Him, giving a concentrated statement of the focus's message.
Commands worship of none but God and grounds it in His sole authority to judge, sharpening the exclusivity in the focus.
Addresses humanity about messengers coming from among them to recite signs, directly clarifying the focus's human, in-community mediation.
Describes a messenger coming from among the addressees and his concern for their hardship, closely developing the focus's phrase about one of them.
Identifies God as Creator and then commands worship of Him, supplying a theological ground for the focus's exclusive call.
Calls communities to worship none but God and reject partners, closely matching the focus's denial of another god.
Decrees worship of none but God and immediately gives its social expression in care for parents.
States worship of God as the created purpose of humans and jinn, giving the focus's command its widest horizon.
Affirms one God and His mercy, providing a concise doctrinal basis for the focus's exclusion of every other god.
A messenger identifies God as his and his audience's Lord and commands worship of Him, closely paralleling the shared-address form.
Commands worship of God without association and extends it into concrete duties toward others.
Questions jinn and humans about messengers from among themselves who recited signs and warned them, reinforcing in-group prophetic address.
Records resistance to worshipping God alone and abandoning inherited objects of worship, a direct contrary reception of the focus's demand.
Commands worship of God alone rather than those worshipped apart from Him, preserving the focus's exclusive contrast.
Begins a messenger's warning with worship of none but God, an especially close prophetic formulation.
A messenger is commanded to worship God without associating partners, linking personal prophetic obedience to the focus's public call.
Reports the objection that a human messenger could not have been sent, directly paralleling the local resistance in 23:33-34.
Identifies God as the shared Lord and commands worship of Him, closely echoing the focus's core message.
Commands steadfast worship of the Lord of the heavens and earth while denying any equal to Him.
A messenger sent to Midian commands worship of God and hope for the Last Day, extending the recurring formula into accountability.
A man urges his people to follow the messengers, adding a recipient-side response to the focus's dispatch.
Rejects worship of others besides God and submits the speaker to the Lord of all worlds, strongly preserving exclusive devotion.
A human messenger announces revelation that the god is one, joining human accessibility with monotheistic proclamation.
Messengers coming before and behind their people command worship of none but God, another broad prophetic precedent.
A messenger names God as his and the audience's Lord and commands worship of Him, matching the focus's shared communal address.
Hud warns his people to worship God alone, directly repeating the prophet-to-community form.
Commands sincere, exclusive worship of God together with prayer and alms, specifying faithful practice of the focus's demand.
Defines messengers as bearers of good news and warning, adding a general purpose of dispatch without the focus's specific message.
God sends revelation with the warning that there is no god but Him, supplying monotheistic content without an in-community messenger.
Mentions God sending messengers and prophets before, broadly supporting the continuity of prophetic dispatch.
Calls people to follow messengers who seek no payment and are guided, offering a recipient-side criterion for response.
Commands worship of God with religion sincerely devoted to Him, a devotional parallel without the messenger setting.
Commands prostration and worship of God, a concise worship response lacking the focus's prophetic address.
Forbids calling on anyone alongside God in places of worship, reinforcing the focus's exclusion of another god.
